original_test_intent: Verify the SMBIOS Type 9 System Slot Data Bus Width enum represents each slot's firmware-advertised bus/lane width, is coherent with slot type and platform wiring, and persists after reboot; it is not the installed device's negotiated PCIe link width.
original_method: Collect complete raw/decoded Type 9 records, preserve the raw width enum with designation, slot ID, type and bus address, compare to the approved physical/electrical slot design, optionally correlate but do not substitute read-only PCI link data, then repeat after reboot.
manual_activity: A user approves the advertised-width map, enum policy and reboot plan. Installing cards or changing link settings is not required; any negotiated-link experiment is separate scope.
required_inputs: Expected SMBIOS data-bus-width enum per Type 9 slot identity
Board/riser slot wiring and bifurcation-capability map
Applicable SMBIOS version and raw width enum definitions
Policy distinguishing slot capability from installed-device negotiated width
Validated parser plus approved reboot/OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS and optional read-only PCI queries; do not force link width/speed, change bifurcation or move adapters.
Preserve raw width byte because x-lane and legacy bit-width enums have different meanings and decoder support varies.
Do not compare the Type 9 advertised slot width directly to a narrower negotiated link without accounting for installed device capability and policy.
Bind width to exact slot ID/designation; an isolated grep line can be assigned to the wrong slot.
Stop on unsupported enum, topology inconsistency, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Decode each Type 9 raw bus-width enum, correlate it with exact slot type/identity and approved wiring, and compare pre/post reboot; collect optional read-only negotiated link data only as separately labeled context.
Do not reconfigure PCIe, manipulate cards or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve advertised-width and wiring/bifurcation expectations, including treatment of narrower installed devices.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The target field is relevant, but grep omits raw enum, slot identity and type/wiring context, so it cannot distinguish an advertised x16 slot from a current x8 device link.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 9 records and compare the raw data-bus-width enum per stable slot identity against the board/riser wiring map; keep any lspci negotiated width in a distinct evidence field.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The System Slot Data Bus Width scope, Type 9 script and 5/5-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.status: ADVERTISED WIDTH AND NEGOTIATED LINK SEPARATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate the version-aware raw Type 9 width enum against platform slot wiring and slot type, while recording optional PCIe LnkCap/LnkSta evidence separately so runtime down-training does not rewrite the SMBIOS expectation.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 9 slots, including legacy bus widths and PCI Express lane-width enums.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, board/riser and dmidecode/parser versions plus PCI tool/version if optional correlation is used.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 9 Slot Data Bus Width enumeration, approved platform wiring specification and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds raw-enum validation and an explicit boundary between advertised slot width and runtime negotiated link width.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; detects firmware metadata errors without false failures caused by a narrower or down-trained installed adapter.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Exact slot wiring/bifurcation map and advertised-versus-negotiated policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Read-only metadata cannot prove all lanes are electrically functional; such validation requires a separate approved hardware/link test.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve narrower configured width for a bifurcated or alternate-riser design, but must bind it to the exact topology and not silently replace slot capability with current LnkSta.
expected_evidence: Approved board/riser revision, slot wiring/bifurcation map, width policy and SMBIOS enum version
Complete pre-reboot Type 9 records with handle, designation, slot ID, raw/decoded width, slot type and supported bus address
Per-slot advertised-width and cross-field comparison; optional negotiated link data separately labeled
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot record diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets the Type 9 advertised data-bus-width field and its persistence.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The width enum is deterministic to collect and compare once the platform map is approved; absence of that map is readiness only.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds raw enum, exact slot identity and advertised-versus-negotiated semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its important width-separation safeguard while correcting the capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Treats missing baselines and reboot approval as readiness inputs, not PARTIAL or BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents false failures when an x16-capable slot negotiates x8 with a specific device and prevents silent acceptance of a decoder label without raw enum provenance.
independent_technical_reasoning: The Type 9 width byte describes slot data-bus capacity as a structured enum; comparison to a topology-specific expected map is a software operation independent of physical link exercise.
